walkthrough: Goal: deliver a piece larger than the canvas, for print or a big screen, with ink lines that stay sharp: export it at two or four times the canvas's size.

Before: on a canvas I ink a closed shape and a line with the Ink Pen, shade with the Pencil, drop the colour into the shape (ColorDrop) and insert a picture as a new layer (Actions > Insert image…, then Transform to place it).

Entry: tap Actions (the spanner in the left island). Under Share, before the save and share rows, one row of three words: 1×, 2× and 4×. 1× carries the ink pill (the default each time the app starts); beside the words, in quieter grey, the file's size in pixels at that scale (the canvas's own size at 1×). Procreate exports at the canvas's size only; the row is ours.

Choose: tap 2×: the pill slides to it and the size doubles (3200 × 1880 here). Tap 4×: the pill slides on, the size reads four times the canvas, and Save JPEG… and Share JPEG… turn pencil grey with the note 'Up to 2×' (a JPEG is encoded whole, so four times the largest canvas would not fit in memory); a tap on them does nothing. Choosing changes nothing in the artwork and is no history step; the panel stays open.

Save: Save PNG… closes the panel and opens the system's save dialog as before ('<title>.png'); choose a folder: 'Saving PNG…' turns while the artwork is rendered at the chosen scale in bands of rows and streamed into the file, then 'Saved “<title>.png”.'. At 2× and 4× the ink lines are drawn anew at that size: their edges are as crisp as at 1× (about one file pixel of antialiasing), never a blown-up copy. The pencil's grain picks the paper's finer level, its tone the same; the fill, the inserted picture and smudges are pictures already, so they are resampled smoothly (the fill's edge stays as stepped as on the canvas, now in larger steps). Every file carries the sRGB profile.
JPEG: back at 2× (or 1×), Save JPEG… writes a JPEG of that size as before.
Cancel and failure: as before (S13): Back in the dialog says nothing; a full disk says so with OK. A 4x export of the largest canvas takes a few seconds; drawing goes on meanwhile.
Undo: exporting and the scale change nothing in the artwork; undo and redo are as before. Reopen: the artwork is unchanged; the scale is back at 1× after the app restarts.
Not here: 8x, a custom size or DPI, a transparent background, exporting layers; the screen still shows the canvas at its own resolution (sharp zoom is S32).
